options: The part of an app that runs on a server and handles data and rules
The bottom half of a web page
quiz.explain: The backend runs on a server: it receives requests, applies the rules, talks to the database and sends back responses.

quiz.q: Which Rust topic should you review before starting this book?
quiz.explain: Ownership shows up on every page of backend code; unsafe, FFI and build scripts are not used in this book.

quiz.q: What does the '### Line by line' part of a lesson give you?
options: What, why and how for each line of the code above it
Only the output of the program
quiz.explain: Each non-trivial line gets What, Why, How and 'Remove it and…' so nothing is magic.

quiz.q: Where is the full, working code for a lesson?
options: Nowhere, you type it from the page
In the code/ folder of the book's repository, linked under each listing
In a zip you email for
quiz.explain: Every listing is included from a real crate in code/, which CI compiles and tests.

flashcards.front: Which crates does this book use for web and database?
flashcards.back: Axum (web framework) and SeaORM (ORM), on top of Tokio (async runtime) and PostgreSQL (database).

flashcards.front: What are the three exercise tiers?
flashcards.back: 🟢 Guided (fill in), 🟡 Tweak (change working code), 🔴 From scratch (write from a one-line spec).
